name: Belly
label: 4AD
lede: Tanya Donelly left her stepsister's band, called three friends from Aquidneck Island, and within two years had a gold record, two Grammy nominations and the cover of Rolling Stone. Then they stopped talking to each other for twenty years.

hero.by: Belly at the 9:30 Club, Washington, D.C., October 2025. Photo: Joe Loong, Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: Siblings, again
eras.text: Tanya Donelly had spent a decade writing the second-string songs in Throwing Muses and a year beside Kim Deal in The Breeders. Belly was the first band where every song was hers, built with three friends from the Newport hardcore scene.

years.src: Martin Aston: Belly, The Birth · Wikipedia: Belly (band)
years.h: Donelly quits Throwing Muses and calls the Gorman brothers
years.p: Tom Gorman on guitar, his brother Chris on drums and [[Fred Abong|d756e807-10da-4fee-9a32-7d76ce120b4b]] on bass. All four knew each other from high school on Aquidneck Island, Rhode Island.
years.xp:
The Gormans had played in the Newport hardcore band Verbal Assault; Abong came out of Vicious Circle and had just spent a year on bass in Throwing Muses. "In our little world, the Muses were rock stars," Chris Gorman told Martin Aston. Donelly liked that the brothers came as a pair: "I'd not been in a band that didn't include siblings."

She named the band Belly because she thought the word was both pretty and ugly.

years.cap: Chris Gorman, Donelly and Tom Gorman in a Sire press photo
years.src: Wikipedia: Belly (band)
years.h: First show: the 3's bar in Newport
years.p: Belly plays its first gig in its hometown. Months later the Slow Dust EP, on 4AD in Britain, goes to No. 1 on the UK indie chart.

years.src: Martin Aston: Belly, The Birth · Vinyl Writer: Interview with Tanya Donelly
years.h: Star splits between Nashville and Liverpool
years.p: Most of the album is cut with Tracy Chisholm in Nashville, then [[Gil Norton|2270fb9d-0f39-4f6f-aba9-ef2bee2f3755]], who'd produced the Muses and [[Pixies|b6b2bb8d-54a9-491f-9607-7b546023b433]], takes over in Liverpool.
years.xp: Partway through the sessions Abong told the band he was leaving. "I said I'd record Star, and then leave," he told Martin Aston. Chris Gorman assumed he'd change his mind: "I thought: what beats doing this?"

eras.title: Buzz Bin, gold and a bassist from a metal band
eras.text: Star came out in the window when alternative radio would play almost anything with a hook. Feed the Tree went to No. 1 on Modern Rock, the video lived on MTV, and a band that had played its first show a year earlier was up for Best New Artist.

years.src: Wikipedia: Feed the Tree · Wikipedia: Star
years.h: Feed the Tree tops the Modern Rock chart
years.p: The single reaches No. 1 on Billboard's Modern Rock Tracks in March and No. 95 on the Hot 100. MTV puts the video in its Buzz Bin.
years.xp: Donelly has said the tree in the song is the place on a big farm where a family buries its dead, and that the song is about commitment and respect. The video picked up two nominations at the 1993 MTV Video Music Awards.

years.cap: Donelly at the Queen Margaret Union, Glasgow, February 1993
years.src: Wikipedia: Star · Wikipedia: Belly (band) · Yorkshire Post: Tanya Donelly
years.h: Star reaches No. 2 in Britain
years.p: 4AD has it out in the UK on January 25, Sire in the US on February 2. In America it goes gold by February 1994.
years.xp: Accounts of what Star sold run from the RIAA's gold (500,000) to Wikipedia's 800,000 in the US; the Yorkshire Post put it at two million worldwide. Gepetto and Slow Dog followed Feed the Tree onto the Modern Rock chart.

years.cap: A fan's 1993 Belly tickets, one for the Radiohead bill at the American Theatre, St. Louis
years.src: Wikipedia: Belly (band) · Belly official bio
years.h: On the road with Radiohead, then the Cranberries opening
years.p: Belly co-headlines a tour with [[Radiohead|a74b1b7f-71a5-4011-9441-d0b5e4122711]], then plays bigger British rooms with The Cranberries in support. [[Leslie Langston|5d9bb2c3-a707-4ef7-a7a3-8fb74776b255]], ex-Throwing Muses, fills in on bass for some dates.

years.src: Martin Aston: Belly, The Birth · Wikipedia: Belly (band)
yt: Dusted and Full Moon, live at Finsbury Park, London, 1993
years.h: Gail Greenwood, a metal guitarist, takes over on bass
years.p: Abong leaves after Star. Greenwood, 24, had let the band rehearse in her basement so she could watch Langston's fingers.
years.xp: Chris Gorman, a surfer, had mentioned the opening to a surfing friend, and the word got to Greenwood. "Gail ushered in a new evolutionary stage," he told Martin Aston. Live, the band got louder and more guitar-heavy, with less of the dream-pop haze of the record.

years.src: Wikipedia: Belly (band) · Wikipedia: Tanya Donelly
years.h: Up for Best New Artist at the Grammys
years.p: Belly is nominated twice: Best New Artist, and Best Alternative Music Performance for Star. They also take home two Boston Music Awards.

eras.title: Surf, storms and Glyn Johns
eras.text: For the second album the band went to the Bahamas with the producer of the Who and the Stones and cut it nearly live. King was louder, the radio climate had turned heavier, and after eighteen months in a van it all came apart.

years.src: It's Psychedelic Baby: Surf, Storms · Yorkshire Post: Tanya Donelly · Martin Aston: Belly, The Birth
years.h: Chris Gorman surfs a waterspout swarm, then nails a take
years.p: Glyn Johns records King at Compass Point in Nassau during tropical storm season. The power keeps cutting out.
years.xp:
"Chris Gorman actually went surfing during a waterspout swarm (do not try this at home)," Donelly told It's Psychedelic Baby, "and then came in and we nailed 'Untitled and Unsung' in two takes." Days ran swim, record, swim, surf, eat fruit, record, then dinner at Johns's place on the water.

Johns had chosen Compass Point, the Yorkshire Post reports, because he'd overextended his US work visa. Tom Gorman said Johns was more the manager's and label's choice than the band's; Donelly fell straight into an easy, family-style rapport with him, while he and Greenwood took longer.

years.src: Wikipedia: King · Martin Aston: Belly, The Birth
years.h: King goes Top 10 in the UK
years.p: No. 6 in Britain and No. 57 in the US. Sales come in far below Star and below what Sire expected.
years.xp: Tom Gorman blamed the label's expectations and the moment: "It was a more male-orientated time, of heavier, grungier guitars." Someone in [[R.E.M.|ea4dfa26-f633-4da6-a52a-f49ea4897b58]] told him King would make sense once Belly had four or five albums behind it. PopMatters later put it at No. 7 on its list of overlooked '90s albums.

years.src: Wikipedia: Belly (band)
years.h: Belly makes the cover of Rolling Stone
years.p: Issue 706. In June the band plays Super-Connected on the Late Show with David Letterman, one of its last big US TV spots.

years.src: Wikipedia: Belly (band) · Belly official bio
yt: Red, The Bees and Untitled & Unsung on Sound FX, June 19, 1995
years.h: Opening for R.E.M. across Europe
years.p: Belly supports [[R.E.M.|ea4dfa26-f633-4da6-a52a-f49ea4897b58]] on the European leg of the Monster tour, then crosses the US with [[Catherine Wheel|37e3dd97-73f9-4c69-b50d-0c0e3c47c40c]] and Jewel opening.

q: I regret not making another Belly album.
years.src: Martin Aston: Belly, The Birth · Yorkshire Post: Tanya Donelly · Wikipedia: Belly (band)
years.h: The last show, then a phone call that never came
years.p: After 18 months on the road, Belly plays what turns out to be its final show. A couple of weeks later, manager Gary Smith tells the Gormans their contracts have expired.
years.xp:
"It felt like we were in a car speeding toward a cliff and nobody could do anything about it," Tom Gorman told Martin Aston. Greenwood says that for the last few months she and the Gormans didn't speak at all, and Tom says Smith wanted Donelly to go solo.

"We didn't have a disaster or death or addiction; we just went our separate ways," Chris Gorman said. "A rookie mistake." Donelly told the Yorkshire Post they should have just taken time off.

years.cap: Ticket for Belly with Catherine Wheel, Commodore Ballroom, Vancouver
years.src: Martin Aston: Belly, The Birth · Wikipedia: Belly (band)
years.h: Donelly ends Belly and goes solo
years.p: Greenwood joins [[L7|57111f1f-9829-45ea-bb4e-a5aba37cd1d1]] almost at once and stays on the road three and a half more years. Tom Gorman plays briefly with [[Buffalo Tom|1159e0d0-a782-471a-9dae-93ac046eac72]].
years.xp: Donelly's Lovesongs for Underdogs came out on 4AD in 1997. Tom Gorman toured with [[Kristin Hersh|0b461f11-c7af-4ddb-a30e-5cb0aabb3e7f]] in 1999, then went into commercial photography in New York with his brother. Abong worked in a high-end woodshop making cabinets and went on to a PhD in philosophy.

eras.title: Maybe we should talk on the phone
eras.text: Chris Gorman spent twenty years floating reunions. What finally worked was Donelly's Swan Song series, which pulled the old bandmates back in one song at a time, and then a tour that turned into a record.

years.src: Martin Aston: Belly, The Birth · Wikipedia: Belly (band)
years.h: The King line-up announces a summer reunion
years.p: "Around 2015, Tanya said, 'Maybe we should talk on the phone,'" Chris Gorman recalled. A new website lists dates in the UK, Ireland and the US.
years.xp: The Swan Song EPs (2013–14) had already brought everyone back into Donelly's orbit: Tom Gorman sent recordings, Greenwood played on a couple of tracks, and Abong co-wrote Snow Goose and Me. "Being back in a room on day one... it instantly erased those months of bad feeling," Greenwood said.

years.cap: Belly in Glasgow on the reunion tour, July 2016
years.src: Wikipedia: Belly (band)
yt: Reunion show at the Royale, Boston, August 2016
years.h: Back home in Newport for two warm-up shows
years.p: Belly's first live dates since 1995. On tour that summer they play two new songs, Human Child and Army of Clay.

years.src: Wikipedia: Belly (band) · Vinyl Writer: Interview with Tanya Donelly
years.h: Fans fund the third album on PledgeMusic
years.p: Belly's first new recording in over 20 years, a cover of Hushabye Mountain, goes to backers that October.

years.cap: Belly's WFUV session at Rockwood Music Hall, New York, May 2018
years.src: Vinyl Writer: Interview with Tanya Donelly · Martin Aston: Belly, The Birth
years.h: Dove, made in basements, bedrooms and closets
years.p: With members spread out, the band trades files instead of sharing a room. It comes out on the band's own Belly Touring label.
years.xp: "That 'all in a room together making noise' vibe is hard to simulate," Tom Gorman told Vinyl Writer. Greenwood called Dove "a great way to heal a rift in the family."

years.src: Wikipedia: Belly (band)
yt: Dove tour, the Garage, Glasgow, June 2018
years.h: A fire moves the Glasgow show overnight
years.p: The Glasgow School of Art fire destroys the O2 ABC the night before. Belly plays the Dove tour date at the Garage instead.

years.src: Martin Aston: Belly, The Birth · Wikipedia: Belly (band)
years.h: 4AD gathers the B-sides as Bees
years.p: Eighteen tracks of B-sides and covers for the 30th anniversary, out for Record Store Day.

eras.title: King turns thirty
eras.text: The record that was supposed to have sunk them got a green-vinyl reissue and its own anniversary tour, with a younger crowd than Belly had in 1995.

years.src: It's Psychedelic Baby: Surf, Storms · Yorkshire Post: Tanya Donelly
years.h: King comes back on green vinyl
years.p: A Record Store Day reissue, remastered by Kevin Vanbergen. "We always loved King, and I still do," Donelly told the Yorkshire Post.

years.cap: Belly at the 9:30 Club, Washington, D.C., October 2025
years.src: Yorkshire Post: Tanya Donelly · Belly official bio
years.h: An anniversary tour, and "a fourth something" on the way
years.p: Belly tours the US and UK for King, reaching Washington's 9:30 Club in October. Donelly says half the new songs are semi-recorded.
